tasks.grade_reason: one default value in a test script and its case
tasks.objective: Backlog topic ci-backlog-followups item 1: tests/routing.test.sh sets WS to the WSL form of the workspace path when RPG_FACTORY_WORKSPACE is unset, so on Git Bash for Windows (uname -s MINGW*/MSYS*/CYGWIN*) the history scenarios and context calls fail unless the variable is exported. When RPG_FACTORY_WORKSPACE is unset, default WS by platform: the drive form under /c/ (same Workspaces/UnityIndie path) on MINGW/MSYS/CYGWIN, the current WSL form elsewhere; export the resolved value as RPG_FACTORY_WORKSPACE for the factory-context.sh calls in the suite that rely on the environment. An explicit RPG_FACTORY_WORKSPACE always wins. When the resolved workspace has no rpg-mmo-server directory, the scenarios that need it already SKIP; keep that. Add a small helper test (a case in tests/routing.test.sh, or a check run by the suite) proving the default resolution for a stubbed uname (MINGW64_NT and Linux) without touching the real workspace. Do not change other suites. Changelog fragment changelog.d/routing-workspace.md (### Fixed).
acceptance: routing.test.sh runs on Git Bash for Windows without RPG_FACTORY_WORKSPACE exported
the default resolution is covered by a test with a stubbed platform

tasks.grade_reason: one detection helper and its test cases
tasks.objective: Backlog topic ci-backlog-followups item 2: scripts/factory-pipeline.py python_alias_line() only checks shutil.which('python3'); when the run lead runs through a python3 shim placed first on PATH, which() finds the shim and the Store-alias line is not printed, although every dispatched session (which starts with a normal PATH) still hits the alias. On win32, also probe the WindowsApps directory directly: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\python3.exe (LOCALAPPDATA from the environment, else the user's home + AppData\Local); if that file exists, print the line naming that path, even when which() resolves elsewhere. Keep: no line on non-win32; no line when neither which() nor the probe finds a WindowsApps python3. Make the probe injectable (a parameter, like platform/which/exe) so tests stay hermetic. Tests in tests/pipeline.test.sh next to the existing python_alias_line cases: shim on PATH plus an existing probed alias file gives the line; shim and no alias file gives no line; non-win32 with the file gives no line. Update changelog.d/dispatch-notes.md only if needed, else add changelog.d/alias-probe.md (### Fixed).
acceptance: the alias line appears when the run lead uses a shim and the Store alias exists
no line without a Store alias or off Windows

tasks.objective: Backlog topic ci-backlog-followups item 3: scripts/lib/pipeline_route.py has _codex_config_path() and a tomllib load inside _codex_auth() that repeat scripts/lib/codexconfig.py home() and config(). Reuse codexconfig: compute the config path from codexconfig.home() (add a small codexconfig.config_path() if that reads better and use it in config() too) and get the parsed data from codexconfig.config() (which returns {} for a missing, unreadable or invalid file and on Python without tomllib). Keep the behaviour and the 'why' strings of _codex_auth() and the cache key in available() (it stats the config path) exactly as now; never print header or key values. Import codexconfig the way other scripts/lib modules import their siblings (both package and flat import forms if pipeline_route needs both). The existing codex-detect cases in tests/pipeline.test.sh must pass unchanged; add one case if a path was not covered (an invalid TOML file means no override). Changelog fragment changelog.d/codex-config-reuse.md (### Changed).
